18. 為了開啟他們的眼睛，使他們從黑暗歸向光明，從 撒旦 的權勢下歸向神，使他們因著信我，罪得赦免，並且與那些被分別為聖的人同得繼業。』 to open their eyes that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a share among those who are sanctified by faith in Me.'
19. 「故此， 阿格里帕 王啊，我沒有悖逆那從天上來的異象。 "Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.
20. 我首先在 大馬士革，然後在 耶路撒冷 、 猶太 全地以及外邦人中，告誡人們要悔改，歸向神，行事與悔改的心相稱。 Instead, I preached to those in Damascus first, and to those in Jerusalem and in all the region of Judea, and to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works worthy of repentance.
21. 猶太 人就是因這緣故，在聖殿裡抓住我，想要殺害我。 For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple complex and were trying to kill me.
22. 然而我蒙了從神而來的幫助，直到今天仍能站立得住，不但向卑微的，還向尊貴的做見證。我所講的，不外乎先知們和 摩西 所說的那些將要成就的事， Since I have obtained help that comes from God, to this day I stand and testify to both small and great, saying nothing else than what the prophets and Moses said would take place--
23. 就是基督要受難，要成為第一個從死人中復活的人，要把光傳給這子民和外邦人。」 that the Messiah must suffer, and that as the first to rise from the dead, He would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles."
24. 保羅 這樣申辯的時候， 菲斯特斯 大聲說：「 保羅，你瘋了！你學問太大，使你癲狂了。」 As he was making his defense this way, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice, "You're out of your mind, Paul! Too much study is driving you mad!"
25. 保羅 說：「 菲斯特斯 大人，我沒有瘋。我說的都是真實、合理的話。 But Paul replied, "I'm not out of my mind, most excellent Festus. On the contrary, I'm speaking words of truth and good judgment.
26. 其實王知道這些事，我才對王放膽直言。我深信這些事沒有一件瞞得過王，因為這不是在角落裡做的。 For the king knows about these matters. It is to him I am actually speaking boldly. For I'm not convinced that any of these things escapes his notice, since this was not done in a corner!
27. 阿格里帕 王啊，您相信先知嗎？我知道您是相信的。」 King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you believe."
28. 阿格里帕 對 保羅 說：「你用幾句話就要說服我成為 基督徒嗎？」 Then Agrippa said to Paul, "Are you going to persuade me to become a Christian so easily?"
29. 保羅 說：「無論話多話少，我向神祈求的，不僅是您，還有今天所有聽我講話的人都能成為像我這樣的人，只是不要有這些鎖鏈！」 "I wish before God," replied Paul, "that whether easily or with difficulty, not only you but all who listen to me today might become as I am-- except for these chains."
30. 於是 王和總督，還有 百妮基 以及與他們坐在一起的人，都站起來了。 So the king, the governor, Bernice, and those sitting with them got up,
31. 當離開的時候，彼此談論說：「這個人沒有做任何該死或該被捆鎖的事。」 and when they had left they talked with each other and said, "This man is doing nothing that deserves death or chains."
32. 阿格里帕 對 菲斯特斯 說：「這個人如果沒有向凱撒上訴，早就可以釋放了。」 Then Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar."
Acts 27
1. 既然決定了我們要坐船往 意大利 去，他們就把 保羅 和其他一些囚犯交給皇家軍團的一個名叫 猶利烏斯 的百夫長。 When it was decided that we were to sail to Italy, they handed over Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Imperial Regiment.
2. 有一條 阿德米提 的船，要開往 亞細亞 省沿岸各地，我們就上那船出發了。有一個從 帖撒羅尼迦 來的 馬其頓 人 亞里達古，與我們在一起。 So when we had boarded a ship of Adramyttium, we put to sea, intending to sail to ports along the coast of the province of Asia. Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, was with us.
3. 第二天，我們在 西頓 靠岸。 猶利烏斯 寬待 保羅，准許他到朋友那裡去接受照顧。 The next day we put in at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul kindly and allowed him to go to his friends to receive their care.
4. 我們從那裡起航，因為逆風，就沿著 塞浦路斯 島的背風岸航行。 When we had put out to sea from there, we sailed along the northern coast of Cyprus because the winds were against us.
5. 度過了 奇里乞亞 省和 潘菲利亞 省一帶的海域，在 呂基亞 省的 每拉 登陸。 After sailing through the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we reached Myra in Lycia.
6. 百夫長在那裡找到了一條 亞歷山大 的船，要開往 意大利 去，就安排我們上了那船。 There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.
7. 一連好幾天，船航行得很慢，好不容易才到了 尼多斯 港附近。因為風攔阻我們往前，我們就從 撒摩尼 岬附近經過，沿著 克里特 島的背風岸航行。 Sailing slowly for many days, we came with difficulty as far as Cnidus. But since the wind did not allow us to approach it, we sailed along the south side of Crete off Salmone.
8. 我們沿著它航行，好不容易來到一個叫做「 美麗港 」的地方；離那裡不遠，有個城叫做 拉塞亞 。 With yet more difficulty we sailed along the coast, and came to a place called Fair Havens near the city of Lasea.
9. 又過了很久，這次航程已經很危險，又因為已經過了禁食日， 保羅 就勸大家， By now much time had passed, and the voyage was already dangerous. Since the Fast was already over, Paul gave his advice
10. 說：「各位，我看這次航程，不僅是貨物和船，就是我們的生命財產也將會受到傷害和嚴重的損失。」 and told them, "Men, I can see that this voyage is headed toward damage and heavy loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives."
11. 可是百夫長信任了船長和船主，不信任 保羅 所說的， But the centurion paid attention to the captain and the owner of the ship rather than to what Paul said.
12. 而且這港口不適合過冬，大多數人就主張從那裡開船，或許能夠到達 菲尼斯 過冬。 菲尼斯 是 克里特 島上的一個港口，一面朝西南，一面朝西北。 Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to set sail from there, hoping somehow to reach Phoenix, a harbor on Crete open to the southwest and northwest, and to winter there.
13. 這時，南風微微吹起，他們以為正合所願，就起了錨，沿著 克里特 島航行。 When a gentle south wind sprang up, they thought they had achieved their purpose; they weighed anchor and sailed along the shore of Crete.
14. 但是過了不久，一股叫做「東北風」的颶風，從島上襲來。 But not long afterwards, a fierce wind called the "northeaster" rushed down from the island.
15. 船被困住，頂不住風，我們只好任憑船被颳走。 Since the ship was caught and was unable to head into the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along.
16. 我們沿著一個叫做 克勞達 小島的背風岸行駛的時候，好不容易才控制住救生艇。 After running under the shelter of a little island called Cauda, we were barely able to get control of the skiff.
17. 水手們 把救生艇拖上來以後，就用纜繩繞過大船底綁好；又怕在 敘爾提斯 淺灘上會擱淺，就把錨放低，任船漂流。 After hoisting it up, they used ropes and tackle and girded the ship. Then, fearing they would run aground on the Syrtis, they lowered the drift-anchor, and in this way they were driven along.
18. 我們被暴風猛烈地襲擊。第二天，他們開始把貨物拋在海裡。 Because we were being severely battered by the storm, they began to jettison the cargo the next day.
19. 第三天，他們又親手把船上的用具拋出去。 On the third day, they threw the ship's gear overboard with their own hands.
20. 一連好幾天見不到太陽和星星，又有暴風雨催逼著，最後我們連獲救的希望都斷絕了。 For many days neither sun nor stars appeared, and the severe storm kept raging; finally all hope that we would be saved was disappearing.
21. 那時，大家已經很久沒有吃東西了， 保羅 站在他們當中說：「哦，各位啊！你們當初應該聽我的，不從 克里特 開船，省得有這樣的傷害和損失。 Since many were going without food, Paul stood up among them and said, "You men should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete and sustain this damage and loss.
22. 只是現在我勸你們振作起來，因為你們當中不會有人失去性命，不過會失去這條船。 Now I urge you to take courage, because there will be no loss of any of your lives, but only of the ship.
23. 要知道，我所歸屬、所事奉的神，他的一位天使昨天晚上站在我身邊， For this night an angel of the God I belong to and serve stood by me,
24. 說：『 保羅，不要怕！你必須站在凱撒面前。看哪，所有與你同船的人，神都賜給你了。』 saying, 'Don't be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. And, look! God has graciously given you all those who are sailing with you.'
25. 所以請各位振作起來，因為我相信神怎樣對我說，事情也會怎樣成就。 Therefore, take courage, men, because I believe God that it will be just the way it was told to me.
26. 不過我們必須擱淺在一個島上。」 However, we must run aground on a certain island."
27. 到了第十四天的晚上，我們在 亞得里亞 海上飄來飄去。約在半夜，水手們認為已經靠近陸地了， When the fourteenth night came, we were drifting in the Adriatic Sea, and in the middle of the night the sailors thought they were approaching land.
28. 就測了水深，發現有三十七公尺 ；稍往前行，再測一測，發現有二十七公尺 。 They took a sounding and found it to be 120 feet deep; when they had sailed a little farther and sounded again, they found it to be 90 feet deep.
29. 他們擔心會撞到礁石，就從船尾拋下四個錨，祈盼著天亮。 Then, fearing we might run aground in some rocky place, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daylight to come.
30. 水手們想離船逃生，就把救生艇放到海裡，卻假裝要從船頭拋錨。 Some sailors tried to escape from the ship; they had let down the skiff into the sea, pretending that they were going to put out anchors from the bow.
31. 保羅 對百夫長和士兵們說：「這些人如果不留在船上，你們就不能獲救。」 Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "Unless these men stay in the ship, you cannot be saved."
32. 於是士兵們就把救生艇的繩索砍斷，由它漂去。 Then the soldiers cut the ropes holding the skiff and let it drop away.
33. 天快亮的時候， 保羅 勸大家用飯，說：「你們一直挨餓等候，什麼都不吃，今天是第十四天了。 When it was just about daylight, Paul urged them all to take food, saying, "Today is the fourteenth day that you have been waiting and going without food, having eaten nothing.
34. 所以我勸你們用飯，因為這是關於你們得救的事。要知道，你們中間，沒有一個人會失去 一根頭髮。」 Therefore I urge you to take some food. For this has to do with your survival, since not a hair will be lost from the head of any of you."
35. 說完這些話， 保羅 就拿起餅，在大家面前感謝神，然後掰開來，開始吃。 After he said these things and had taken some bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of them all, and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
36. 於是大家受到鼓勵，也吃了飯。 They all became encouraged and took food themselves.
37. 我們在船上的，共有兩百七十六個人 。 In all there were 276 of us on the ship.
38. 大家吃飽了飯，就把麥子扔到海裡，減輕船的負荷。 And having eaten enough food, they began to lighten the ship by throwing the grain overboard into the sea.
39. 天亮的時候，他們雖然不認識那地方，卻看見一個有沙灘的海灣，就決定盡可能地把船攏進去。 When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but sighted a bay with a beach. They planned to run the ship ashore if they could.
40. 於是他們砍斷了錨，把它們丟棄在海裡，同時鬆開舵繩，拉起了前帆，順著風向岸前進。 After casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time loosening the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and headed for the beach.
41. 但遇到海水夾流的地方，船就擱了淺，船頭被卡住，動彈不得，而船尾也開始被波浪的猛力衝散了。 But they struck a sandbar and ran the ship aground. The bow jammed fast and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up with the pounding of the waves.
42. 士兵們的計劃是要把囚犯殺了，免得有人游泳逃脫。 The soldiers' plan was to kill the prisoners so that no one could swim off and escape.
43. 可是百夫長想救 保羅，就攔阻了他們的計劃，命令會游泳的人跳下船，先到岸上去， But the centurion kept them from carrying out their plan because he wanted to save Paul, so he ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
44. 其餘的人，有的用木板，有的用船上的東西跟著 ；這樣，大家就都獲救上岸了。 The rest were to follow, some on planks and some on debris from the ship. In this way, all got safely to land.
Acts 28
1. 我們獲救以後才知道那島叫做 馬耳他， Safely ashore, we then learned that the island was called Malta.
2. 那裡的土人對我們非常友善。因為當時下著雨，又因為天氣冷，他們就生了火接待我們大家。 The local people showed us extraordinary kindness, for they lit a fire and took us all in, since rain was falling and it was cold.
3. 保羅 收集了一捆柴火，放在火堆上的時候，有一條毒蛇因熱鑽了出來，咬住 他的手。 As Paul gathered a bundle of brushwood and put it on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened itself to his hand.
4. 那些土人一看見那毒蛇懸在他的手上，就彼此說：「這個人一定是個殺人犯！雖然從海裡獲救了，但天理還是不讓他活著。」 When the local people saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, "This man is probably a murderer, and though he has escaped the sea, Justice does not allow him to live!"
5. 可是 保羅 把那毒蛇甩在火裡，沒有受任何傷害。 However, he shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no harm.
6. 他們本來以為他快要腫起來，或是突然倒下死去，然而等了很久，看見他沒有任何異常，就改變了想法，說他是個神。 They expected that he would swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after they waited a long time and saw nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
7. 在那個地方附近，有些田產是島上首領 普布利烏 的。他歡迎我們，熱情地招待了我們三天。 Now in the area around that place was an estate belonging to the leading man of the island, named Publius, who welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
8. 當時， 普布利烏 的父親患熱病和痢疾，躺在床上 。 保羅 就進去為他禱告，按手在他身上，使他痊癒了。 It happened that Publius' father was in bed suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went to him, and praying and laying his hands on him, he healed him.
9. 這麼一來，島上其他有病的人也都來了，並且都得了痊癒。 After this, the rest of those on the island who had diseases also came and were cured.
10. 他們十分尊重我們；開船的時候，還送上所需要的東西。 So they heaped many honors on us, and when we sailed, they gave us what we needed.
11. 過了三個月，我們上了一條 亞歷山大 的船起航。這船是在那海島過冬的，以「 宙斯 雙子神」為船頭雕像。 After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered at the island, with the Twin Brothers as its figurehead.
12. 我們在 敘拉古 靠岸，停留了三天， Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed three days.
13. 又從那裡繞道航行，到達 利基翁 。過了一天，颳起了南風，第二天我們就到了 普特奧利， From there, after making a circuit along the coast, we reached Rhegium. After one day a south wind sprang up, and the second day we came to Puteoli.
14. 在那裡找到一些弟兄，受邀請與他們同住了七天。 這樣，我們來到了 羅馬 。 There we found believers and were invited to stay with them for seven days. And so we came to Rome.
15. 那裡的弟兄們聽說了有關我們的事，趕到 阿比烏 市場和 三館 來迎接我們。 保羅 見到他們，就感謝神，得了勇氣。 Now the believers from there had heard the news about us and had come to meet us as far as Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
16. 我們進了 羅馬 以後， 保羅 獲准在一個士兵的看守之下，獨自居住。 And when we entered Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.
17. 第三天， 保羅 請 猶太 人的首領們來。他們聚集了， 保羅 就對他們說：「各位兄弟，我沒有做過任何反對我們民族或先祖規矩的事，卻做為囚犯從 耶路撒冷 被交到 羅馬 人手中。 After three days he called together the leaders of the Jews. And when they had gathered he said to them: "Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our forefathers, I was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans
18. 他們審問我以後，因為沒有處死我的任何理由，本來想要釋放我。 who, after examining me, wanted to release me, since I had not committed a capital offense.
19. 但是由於 猶太 人反對，我被迫向凱撒上訴，並不是有什麼事要控告自己的同胞。 Because the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar; it was not as though I had any accusation against my nation.
20. 因這理由，我請你們來見面談話。其實我是為了 以色列 所盼望的事，才被這鎖鏈捆鎖的。」 So, for this reason I've asked to see you and speak to you. In fact, it is for the hope of Israel that I'm wearing this chain."
21. 他們對 保羅 說：「我們沒有收到從 猶太 來的有關你的文件。來到這裡的同胞 中，也沒有人報告過或說過任何有關你的壞事。 And they said to him, "We haven't received any letters about you from Judea; none of the brothers has come and reported or spoken anything evil about you.
22. 不過我們覺得應該聽聽你的想法，因為我們確實知道有關這教派的事，它到處遭人反對。」 But we consider it suitable to hear from you what you think. For concerning this sect, we are aware that it is spoken against everywhere."
23. 於是他們和 保羅 定好了日子，就有更多的人來到他的住所。 保羅 從早到晚對他們講解，為神的國鄭重地做見證，並且引用 摩西 的律法和先知書上有關耶穌的事來勸導他們。 After arranging a day with him, many came to him at his lodging. From dawn to dusk he expounded and witnessed about the kingdom of God. He persuaded them concerning Jesus from both the Law of Moses and the Prophets.
24. 對他所說的話，有些人信從了，有些人卻不相信。 Some were persuaded by what he said, but others did not believe.
25. 他們彼此不一致，開始散去， 保羅 就說了一句話：「聖靈藉著先知 以賽亞 對你們 祖先所說的是對的。 Disagreeing among themselves, they began to leave after Paul made one statement: "The Holy Spirit correctly spoke through the prophet Isaiah to your forefathers
26. 他說： 『你去告訴這子民： 你們將聽了又聽，但絕不會領悟； 你們將看了又看，但絕不會明白； when He said, Go to this people and say: 'You will listen and listen, yet never understand; and you will look and look, yet never perceive.
27. 因為這子民的心麻木了， 他們充耳不聞，眼睛閉著； 免得他們眼睛看見，耳朵聽見，心裡領悟， 回轉過來，我就使他們痊癒。』 For this people's heart has grown callous, their ears are hard of hearing, and they have shut their eyes; otherwise they might see with their eyes and hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and be converted-- and I would heal them.'
28. 所以你們應當知道：神的這救恩已經傳給了外邦人，他們反倒會聽！」 Therefore, let it be known to you that this saving work of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will listen!"
29. 保羅 說完這些話， 猶太 人就走了，彼此議論紛紛。 [[After he said these things, the Jews departed, while engaging in a prolonged debate among themselves.]]
30. 保羅 在自己租的房子裡住了整整兩年，所有來到他那裡的人，他都歡迎。 Then he stayed two whole years in his own rented house. And he welcomed all who visited him,
31. 他宣講神的國、教導有關主耶穌基督的事，滿有膽量、沒有攔阻。 proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with full boldness and without hindrance.
Romans
Romans 1
1. 我 保羅 做基督耶穌的奴僕、蒙召的使徒，是為了神的福音被分別出來的。 Paul, a slave of Christ Jesus, called as an apostle and singled out for God's good news--
2. 這福音是神先前藉著他的先知們，在聖經上所應許的， which He promised long ago through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures--
3. 是關於他的兒子——我們的主耶穌基督的。照著肉身說，他出自 大衛 的後裔； concerning His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh
4. 照著聖潔的靈 說，藉著從死人中復活，他被顯明是神大能的兒子。 and was established as the powerful Son of God by the resurrection from the dead according to the Spirit of holiness.
5. 我們從他領受了恩典和使徒的職份，為了他名的緣故，要在萬民中帶來信仰上的順從； We have received grace and apostleship through Him to bring about the obedience of faith among all the nations, on behalf of His name,
6. 其中也有你們這些蒙召喚、屬耶穌基督的人。 including yourselves who are also Jesus Christ's by calling:
7. 致所有在 羅馬 、蒙神所愛、蒙召成為聖徒的人： 願恩典與平安從神我們的父和主耶穌基督臨到你們！ To all who are in Rome, loved by God, called as saints. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
8. 首先，我藉著耶穌基督，為你們各位感謝我的神，因為你們的忠信被傳遍全世界。 First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you because the news of your faith is being reported in all the world.
9. 事實上，神——就是我在他兒子的福音工作上用心靈所事奉的那一位，可以為我見證：我怎樣不住地提到你們， For God, whom I serve with my spirit in [telling] the good news about His Son, is my witness that I constantly mention you,
10. 在我的禱告中總是祈求，或許可以照著神的旨意，終有一天能順利地到你們那裡去； always asking in my prayers that if it is somehow in God's will, I may now at last succeed in coming to you.
11. 因為我切切地想見到你們，好把一些屬靈的恩賜分給你們，使你們得以堅固。 For I want very much to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,
12. 這就是說，在你們那裡，藉著你們和我裡面彼此的信仰，大家可以同得鼓勵。 that is, to be mutually encouraged by each other's faith, both yours and mine.
13. 弟兄們，我不願意你們不明白：我多次計劃到你們那裡去，為要在你們那裡也得一些果實，就像我在其他外邦人中那樣，可是直到如今還受到攔阻。 Now I want you to know, brothers, that I often planned to come to you (but was prevented until now) in order that I might have a fruitful ministry among you, just as among the rest of the Gentiles.
14. 無論是 希臘 人或是外族人，有智慧的或是無知的，我都對他們有責任 。 I am obligated both to Greeks and barbarians, both to the wise and the foolish.
15. 因此，我願意盡我所能，把福音也傳給你們在 羅馬 的人。 So I am eager to preach the good news to you also who are in Rome.
16. 的確，我不以 福音為恥，因為這福音是神的大能，把救恩帶給一切相信的人，先是 猶太 人、後是外邦人 。 For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is God's power for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, and also to the Greek.
17. 原來，神的義就在這福音上顯明出來——本於信，以至於信，正如經上所記： 「義人將因信而活。」 For in it God's righteousness is revealed from faith to faith, just as it is written: The righteous will live by faith.
18. 要知道，人用不公義抵擋真理，神的震怒就從天上顯明在人的一切不敬虔和不公義上。 For God's wrath is revealed from heaven against all godlessness and unrighteousness of people who by their unrighteousness suppress the truth,
19. 實際上，有關神的事，人所能知道的，在他們裡面是清清楚楚的，因為神已經向他們顯明了。 since what can be known about God is evident among them, because God has shown it to them.
20. 原來，自從創世以來，神那不可見的本性，就是他永恆的大能和神性，都藉著所造之物，被人明白、被人看見，以致使人無法推諉。 From the creation of the world His invisible attributes, that is, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood through what He has made. As a result, people are without excuse.
21. 所以人是已經知道神的，但是卻不把他當做神來榮耀他，也不感謝他；相反，他們在思想上變得虛妄，他們無知的心就昏暗了。 For though they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God or show gratitude. Instead, their thinking became nonsense, and their senseless minds were darkened.
22. 他們自稱是有智慧的，卻成了愚拙， Claiming to be wise, they became fools
23. 甚至用偶像，就是會朽壞的人、飛禽、走獸、爬行動物的形像，來取代那不朽之神的榮耀。 and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal man, birds, four-footed animals, and reptiles.
24. 因此，神任憑他們順著心中的情欲去做汙穢的事，以致彼此玷汙自己的身體。 Therefore God delivered them over in the cravings of their hearts to sexual impurity, so that their bodies were degraded among themselves.
25. 他們用虛假取代神的真理，去崇拜、事奉被造之物，而不事奉造物之主——主是當受頌讚的，直到永遠！阿們。 They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served something created instead of the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
26. 為此，神任憑他們陷入可恥的情欲，連他們的女人也把天性的功用變為違反天性的； This is why God delivered them over to degrading passions. For even their females exchanged natural sexual intercourse for what is unnatural.
27. 同樣，男人也放棄了女人天性的功用，彼此之間欲火中燒，男人與男人做出羞恥的事，就在自己身上 受到他們的妄為 所應得的報應。 The males in the same way also left natural sexual intercourse with females and were inflamed in their lust for one another. Males committed shameless acts with males and received in their own persons the appropriate penalty for their perversion.
28. 既然人不願意真正認識神，神就任憑他們存敗壞的理性，去做那些不該做的事。 And because they did not think it worthwhile to have God in their knowledge, God delivered them over to a worthless mind to do what is morally wrong.
29. 他們充滿了各種不義、 邪惡、貪心、惡毒；滿心是嫉妒、凶殺、紛爭、欺詐、狠毒；他們搬弄是非、 They are filled with all unrighteousness, evil, greed, and wickedness. They are full of envy, murder, disputes, deceit, and malice. They are gossips,
30. 誹謗人、憎恨神、侮慢人、驕傲、自誇、製造惡行、悖逆父母、 slanderers, God-haters, arrogant, proud, boastful, inventors of evil, disobedient to parents,
31. 愚昧無知、不守信用、沒有親情、 毫無憐憫。 undiscerning, untrustworthy, unloving, and unmerciful.
32. 人雖然知道神的公義規定是：行這樣事的人是該死的；然而他們不僅自己去做，還贊同做這些事的人。 Although they know full well God's just sentence-- that those who practice such things deserve to die-- they not only do them, but even applaud others who practice them.
Romans 2
1. 哦，人哪，所以你是無法推諉的！一切評斷人的啊，你在什麼事上評斷別人，就在什麼事上定自己的罪；因為你這評斷人的，你自己也在做同樣的事。 Therefore, anyone of you who judges is without excuse. For when you judge another, you condemn yourself, since you, the judge, do the same things.
2. 況且我們知道，對做這樣事的人，神是按照真理來審判他們的。 We know that God's judgment on those who do such things is based on the truth.
3. 哦，人哪！你評斷做這樣事的人，而自己也做同樣的事，你以為你能逃脫神的審判嗎？ Do you really think-- anyone of you who judges those who do such things yet do the same-- that you will escape God's judgment?
4. 難道你輕視神豐富的仁慈、寬容、耐心，不明白他的仁慈是引領你來悔改的嗎？ Or do you despise the riches of His kindness, restraint, and patience, not recognizing that God's kindness is intended to lead you to repentance?
5. 可是你照著頑固和不悔改的心，為那震怒的日子，就是神公義審判顯現的日子，給自己積蓄了震怒。 But because of your hardness and unrepentant heart you are storing up wrath for yourself in the day of wrath, when God's righteous judgment is revealed.
6. 神將照著各人的行為回報各人 ： He will repay each one according to his works:
7. 對那些恆心行善，尋求榮耀、尊貴、不朽的，就以永恆的生命回報他們； eternal life to those who by patiently doing good seek for glory, honor, and immortality;
8. 而對那些營私爭競 、不肯信從真理、反信從不義的，就以震怒和憤恨回報他們。 but wrath and indignation to those who are self-seeking and disobey the truth, but are obeying unrighteousness;
9. 神要把患難和困苦加給一切作惡之人的靈魂，先是 猶太 人的，後是外邦人 的； affliction and distress for every human being who does evil, first to the Jew, and also to the Greek;
10. 而把榮耀、尊貴、平安賜給所有做美善事的人，先是 猶太 人，後是外邦人 。 but glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first to the Jew, and also to the Greek.
11. 要知道，神是不偏待人的。 There is no favoritism with God.
12. 凡是在律法之外犯過罪的，也將要在律法之外滅亡；凡是在律法之下犯過罪的，將要照著律法受審判。 All those who sinned without the law will also perish without the law, and all those who sinned under the law will be judged by the law.
13. 因為在神面前，不是律法的聽者為義，而是律法的實行者被稱為義。 For the hearers of the law are not righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be declared righteous.
14. 其實沒有律法的外邦人，一旦按照本性去行律法上的事，他們雖然沒有律法，但自己就是自己的律法了。 So, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, instinctively do what the law demands, they are a law to themselves even though they do not have the law.
15. 這就顯出律法的要求 刻在他們的心裡，他們的良心也一同作證，而且自己的心思之間，互相控告或辯解。 They show that the work of the law is written on their hearts. Their consciences testify in support of this, and their competing thoughts either accuse or excuse them
16. 正如我的福音，這些事要在那日，神藉著基督耶穌審判各人隱祕事的時候，顯明出來。 on the day when God judges what people have kept secret, according to my gospel through Christ Jesus.
17. 你既然 稱為 猶太 人，依靠律法，以神誇耀； Now if you call yourself a Jew, and rest in the law, and boast in God,
18. 又從律法中受教，明白神的 旨意，也能分辨是非 ； and know His will, and approve the things that are superior, being instructed from the law,
19. 又深信自己是瞎子的領路人，是在黑暗中人的光， and are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light to those in darkness,
20. 是愚妄人的導師，是小孩子的教師，擁有著律法上知識和真理的規範， an instructor of the ignorant, a teacher of the immature, having in the law the full expression of knowledge and truth--
21. 那麼，你這教導別人的，難道不教導自己嗎？你這宣講不可偷竊的，難道自己還偷竊嗎？ you then, who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who preach, "You must not steal"-- do you steal?
22. 你這說不可通姦的，難道自己還通姦嗎？你這憎惡偶像的，難道自己還偷取廟裡的東西嗎？ You who say, "You must not commit adultery"-- do you commit adultery? You who detest idols, do you rob their temples?
23. 你這以律法誇耀的，難道自己還違犯律法侮辱神嗎？ You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
24. 事實上，正如經上所記： 「因你們的緣故，神的名在外邦人中受到褻瀆。」 For, as it is written: The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.
25. 你如果是遵行律法的，割禮才有益處；但你如果是違犯律法的人，你的割禮就不是割禮了。 For circumcision benefits you if you observe the law, but if you are a lawbreaker, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
26. 因此，那沒有受割禮的人，如果遵守律法的公義規定，他雖然沒有受割禮，難道不是算是受了割禮嗎？ Therefore if an uncircumcised man keeps the law's requirements, will his uncircumcision not be counted as circumcision?
27. 並且，那生來沒有受割禮卻完全實行律法的人，對你這雖有律法條文和割禮卻違犯律法的人，難道不是要施行審判嗎？ A man who is physically uncircumcised, but who fulfills the law, will judge you who are a lawbreaker in spite of having the letter [of the law] and circumcision.
28. 其實外表上做 猶太 人的，並不是 猶太 人；外表上、肉身上的割禮，也不是割禮。 For a person is not a Jew who is one outwardly, and [true] circumcision is not something visible in the flesh.
29. 然而，在內心做 猶太 人的才是 猶太 人；同樣，內心的割禮才是割禮——不是靠著律法條文而是靠著聖靈；這樣的人得到的稱讚不是從人來的，而是從神來的。 On the contrary, a person is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is of the heart-- by the Spirit, not the letter. His praise is not from men but from God.
Romans 3
1. 這樣說來， 猶太 人有什麼優越呢？割禮有什麼益處呢？ So what advantage does the Jew have? Or what is the benefit of circumcision?
2. 在各方面都有很多。首要的，是神的話語確實委託給他們了。 Considerable in every way. First, they were entrusted with the spoken words of God.
3. 即使他們中有些人不信，到底又怎麼樣呢？難道他們的不信會使神的信實無效嗎？ What then? If some did not believe, will their unbelief cancel God's faithfulness?
4. 絕對不會！即使每個人都是說謊者，神還是真實的。正如經上所記： 「這樣，你說話的時候，顯為公義； 被評斷的時候，必然得勝。」 Absolutely not! God must be true, but everyone is a liar, as it is written: That You may be justified in Your words and triumph when You judge.
5. 但是，如果我按人的意思來說，我們的不義可以顯明神的義，那我們要怎麼說呢？難道降震怒的神是不公正的嗎？ But if our unrighteousness highlights God's righteousness, what are we to say? I use a human argument: Is God unrighteous to inflict wrath?
6. 絕對不是！否則，神怎麼能審判世界呢？ Absolutely not! Otherwise, how will God judge the world?
7. 那麼，如果神的真實因我的虛謊使他的榮耀更加豐盛，為什麼我還要像罪人一樣被定罪呢？ But if by my lie God's truth is amplified to His glory, why am I also still judged as a sinner?
8. 這樣，為什麼不說「讓我們作惡好帶來善」呢？——我們正是如此受到毀謗，也有些人說過我們講了這話——這些人被定罪倒是應該的。 And why not say, just as some people slanderously claim we say, "Let us do evil so that good may come"? Their condemnation is deserved!
9. 那麼怎麼樣呢？我們 猶太 人比別人好嗎？當然不是！我們已經指出： 猶太 人和外邦人 都在罪孽之下。 What then? Are we any better? Not at all! For we have previously charged that both Jews and Gentiles are all under sin,
10. 正如經上所記： 「沒有義人，連一個也沒有； as it is written: There is no one righteous, not even one;
11. 沒有領悟的， 沒有尋求神的。 there is no one who understands, there is no one who seeks God.
12. 人人都遠離了正道， 一同成了無用的； 沒有仁慈的， 連一個也沒有。 All have turned away, together they have become useless; there is no one who does good, there is not even one.
13. 他們的喉嚨是敞開的墳墓， 他們用舌頭玩弄詭詐， 他們的嘴唇含有蛇毒， Their throat is an open grave; they deceive with their tongues. Vipers' venom is under their lips.
14. 他們滿口是咒罵和苦毒， Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.
15. 他們的腳步為殺人 流血而飛快， Their feet are swift to shed blood;
16. 他們的路 上 只有毀滅和慘禍； ruin and wretchedness are in their paths,
17. 和平之路，他們從來不知道。 and the path of peace they have not known.
18. 他們的眼目中沒有對神的敬畏。 」 There is no fear of God before their eyes.
19. 我們知道，律法上的一切話都是對律法之下的人講的，好堵住每個人的口，使全世界的人都在神的審判之下有罪， Now we know that whatever the law says speaks to those who are subject to the law, so that every mouth may be shut and the whole world may become subject to God's judgment.
20. 因為沒有一個人 本於律法上的行為在神面前被稱為義；原來，藉著律法，只能對罪有真正的認識。 For no flesh will be justified in His sight by the works of the law, for through the law [comes] the knowledge of sin.
21. 但如今，神的義已經在律法之外顯明出來，被律法和先知們所見證， But now, apart from the law, God's righteousness has been revealed-- attested by the Law and the Prophets
22. 那就是：神的義藉著對耶穌基督的信仰，臨到所有信的人，並沒有分別。 -- that is, God's righteousness through faith in Jesus Christ, to all who believe, since there is no distinction.
23. 要知道，每個人都犯了罪，虧缺了神的榮耀； For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
24. 但藉著神的恩典，藉著在基督耶穌裡的救贖，卻無償地被稱為義。 They are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
25. 神預先定下耶穌為平息祭，是用耶穌的血、藉著人的信，為要顯明神自己的義；因為他用忍耐的心，寬容人過去所犯的罪， God presented Him as a propitiation through faith in His blood, to demonstrate His righteousness, because in His restraint God passed over the sins previously committed.
26. 為了在現今的時刻顯明他的義，好表明他自己為義，也稱信耶穌的人為義。 He presented Him to demonstrate His righteousness at the present time, so that He would be righteous and declare righteous the one who has faith in Jesus.
27. 既然如此，還有什麼可誇耀的呢？根本沒有。憑著什麼法則呢？憑著行為的法則嗎？不是！而是憑著信的法則。 Where then is boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? By one of works? No, on the contrary, by a law of faith.
28. 就是說，我們認為：人被稱為義，是藉著信，與律法上的行為無關。 For we conclude that a man is justified by faith apart from works of law.
29. 難道神只是 猶太 人的神嗎？不也是外邦人的神嗎？是的，他也是外邦人的神， Or is God for Jews only? Is He not also for Gentiles? Yes, for Gentiles too,
30. 既然神真是一位；他要使受割禮的人因信稱義，也要使沒有受割禮的人因信稱義。 since there is one God who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith.
31. 那麼，我們是藉著信廢掉律法嗎？絕對不是！反而確立了律法。 Do we then cancel the law through faith? Absolutely not! On the contrary, we uphold the law.
Romans 4
1. 那麼，我們說我們肉體上的先祖 亞伯拉罕 得到了什麼呢？ What then can we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found?
2. 事實上，如果 亞伯拉罕 本於行為被稱為義，他就有可誇耀的；然而在神面前他並沒有可誇耀的。 If Abraham was justified by works, then he has something to brag about-- but not before God.
3. 經上到底是怎麼說的呢？ 「 亞伯拉罕 信神， 這就被算為他的義。」 For what does the Scripture say? Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him for righteousness.
4. 做工的人得工錢，不算是恩典，而是應得的； Now to the one who works, pay is not considered as a gift, but as something owed.
5. 但是，一個人雖沒有做工，卻信靠那稱不敬虔之人為義的神，這人的信就被算為義。 But to the one who does not work, but believes on Him who declares righteous the ungodly, his faith is credited for righteousness.
6. 正如 大衛 也論到神所算為義之人的福份，這義與行為無關；他說： Likewise, David also speaks of the blessing of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
7. 「罪惡 被赦免、 罪孽被遮蓋的人， 這人是蒙福的。 How happy those whose lawless acts are forgiven and whose sins are covered!
8. 主絕不算為有罪的， 這人是蒙福的。」 How happy the man whom the Lord will never charge with sin!
9. 既然如此，這福份到底是只賜給那些受割禮的人，還是也賜給那些沒有受割禮的人呢？我們說： 「 亞伯拉罕 因著信，就被算為義了。」 Is this blessing only for the circumcised, then? Or is it also for the uncircumcised? For we say, Faith was credited to Abraham for righteousness.
10. 那麼，是怎麼被算為義的呢？到底是在他受割禮之後，還是在他沒有受割禮的時候呢？不是在受割禮之後，而是在沒有受割禮的時候。 How then was it credited-- while he was circumcised, or uncircumcised? Not while he was circumcised, but uncircumcised.
11. 並且他領受了割禮的標記，做為他沒有受割禮時因信稱義的印證，使他成為所有不憑著割禮而信之人的父，也使他們被算為義； And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while still uncircumcised. This was to make him the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, so that righteousness may be credited to them also.
12. 而且他也成為受割禮之人的父，不僅為那些受了割禮的人，還為那些順著我們的先祖 亞伯拉罕 信心之腳蹤行走的人； 亞伯拉罕 的信心在他沒有受割禮的時候就已經有了。 And he became the father of the circumcised, not only to those who are circumcised, but also to those who follow in the footsteps of the faith our father Abraham had while still uncircumcised.
13. 原來，賜給 亞伯拉罕 和他後裔繼承世界的應許，不是藉著律法，而是藉著因信而得的義。 For the promise to Abraham or to his descendants that he would inherit the world was not through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.
14. 這是因為，如果本於律法的才是繼承人，信就落了空，應許也就無效了。 If those who are of the law are heirs, faith is made empty and the promise is canceled.
15. 事實上，律法帶來了震怒，所以哪裡沒有律法，哪裡也就沒有過犯。 For the law produces wrath; but where there is no law, there is no transgression.
16. 為此，這應許是本於信，好使這應許照著恩典，能確保給所有的後裔——不僅是給屬律法的，也是給屬 亞伯拉罕 信心的。 亞伯拉罕 在神面前是我們每個人的父， This is why the promise is by faith, so that it may be according to grace, to guarantee it to all the descendants-- not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of Abraham's faith. He is the father of us all
17. 正如經上所記： 「我已經指派你為眾多民族的父。」 亞伯拉罕 所信的那一位，就是叫死人得生命、使無變為有的神。 in God's sight. As it is written: I have made you the father of many nations. He believed in God, who gives life to the dead and calls things into existence that do not exist.
18. 亞伯拉罕 在沒有盼望的時候，仍然懷著盼望去相信，因而成為 眾多民族的父， 正如先前所說： 「你的後裔將要如此眾多 。」 Against hope, with hope he believed, so that he became the father of many nations, according to what had been spoken: So will your descendants be.
19. 他快到一百歲的時候，想到自己的身體如同 已經死了，又想到 撒拉 也已經不能生育，但是他的信仰卻沒有軟弱。 He considered his own body to be already dead (since he was about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah's womb, without weakening in the faith.
20. 他也沒有因著不信去懷疑神的應許，反而因著信得以剛強，把榮耀歸給神， He did not waver in unbelief at God's promise, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,
21. 並且確信不疑：神所應許的，神也能成就。 because he was fully convinced that what He had promised He was also able to perform.
22. 因此，這就被算為他的義了。 Therefore, it was credited to him for righteousness.
23. 不但如此， 「被算為他的義」 這句話不僅是為 亞伯拉罕 寫的， Now it was credited to him was not written for Abraham alone,
24. 也是為我們寫的；我們信靠使我們的主耶穌從死人中復活的那一位，就將被算為義。 but also for us. It will be credited to us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
25. 主耶穌被交出去，是為了我們的過犯；復活，是為了我們稱義。 He was delivered up for our trespasses and raised for our justification.
Romans 5
1. 這樣，我們既然因信稱義，就藉著我們的主耶穌基督與神和好了； Therefore, since we have been declared righteous by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
2. 我們也藉著他，因信 進入了現在所站的這恩典中，並且以盼望神的榮耀而誇耀。 Also through Him, we have obtained access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.
3. 不僅如此，我們也以患難誇耀，因為我們知道患難生出忍耐， And not only that, but we also rejoice in our afflictions, because we know that affliction produces endurance,
4. 忍耐生出品德，品德生出盼望， endurance produces proven character, and proven character produces hope.
5. 而這盼望不使人羞愧，因為神的愛藉著所賜給我們的聖靈，已經傾注在我們的心裡。 This hope does not disappoint, because God's love has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
6. 原來，當我們還軟弱的時候，基督就按照所定的時候為不敬虔的人死了。 For while we were still helpless, at the appointed moment, Christ died for the ungodly.
7. 為義人死，是少有的；為好人死，或許有敢做的； For rarely will someone die for a just person-- though for a good person perhaps someone might even dare to die.
8. 但是，當我們還是罪人的時候，基督就替我們死了。神的愛就在此向我們顯明了。 But God proves His own love for us in that while we were still sinners Christ died for us!
9. 所以，我們現在既然藉著基督的血被稱為義，難道不更要藉著他，從神的 震怒中被拯救出來嗎？ Much more then, since we have now been declared righteous by His blood, we will be saved through Him from wrath.
10. 這樣，我們做神敵人的時候，尚且能藉著神兒子的死與神和好，何況和好以後，難道不更要藉著神兒子的生命得救嗎？ For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son, [then how] much more, having been reconciled, will we be saved by His life!
11. 不僅如此，我們現在藉著主耶穌基督與神 和好了，就更要藉著他以神誇耀。 And not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
12. 所以，正如罪是藉著一個人進入了世界，並且死是藉著罪進入的；這樣，因為人人都犯了罪，死也就臨到了所有的人。 Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, in this way death spread to all men, because all sinned.
13. 就是說，沒有律法以前，罪已經在世上了；不過沒有律法，罪就不算為罪。 In fact, sin was in the world before the law, but sin is not charged to one's account when there is no law.
14. 然而，從 亞當 到 摩西，死亡掌了權，甚至那些沒有按 亞當 過犯的樣式犯罪的人，也在死的權下。這 亞當 是以後要來的那一位的象徵。 Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over those who did not sin in the likeness of Adam's transgression. He is a prototype of the Coming One.
15. 但是恩賜不同於過犯。原來，一個人的過犯尚且使眾人都死了，何況神的恩典和耶穌基督一個人恩典裡的賞賜，難道不更要豐豐富富地臨到眾人嗎？ But the gift is not like the trespass. For if by the one man's trespass the many died, how much more have the grace of God and the gift overflowed to the many by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ.
16. 而且，恩賜不同於由一個人犯罪而來的後果 。因為，由一次過犯而來的審判雖然導致了定罪，但由很多過犯而來的恩賜卻導致了稱義。 And the gift is not like the one man's sin, because from one sin came the judgment, resulting in condemnation, but from many trespasses came the gift, resulting in justification.
17. 實際上，一個人的過犯尚且使死亡藉著這一個人掌了權，何況那些領受豐富之恩典和稱義之賞賜的人，難道不更要藉著耶穌基督一個人，在生命裡掌權嗎？ Since by the one man's trespass, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive the overflow of grace and the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ.
18. 由此可見，藉著一次的過犯導致了所有人的定罪；照樣，藉著一次的義行給所有的人帶來永生的 稱義。 So then, as through one trespass there is condemnation for everyone, so also through one righteous act there is life-giving justification for everyone.
19. 就是說，藉著一個人的悖逆，眾人怎樣都成了罪人；藉著一個人的順從，眾人將怎樣成為義人。 For just as through one man's disobedience the many were made sinners, so also through the one man's obedience the many will be made righteous.
20. 律法出現，為要使過犯增多；可是，罪在哪裡增多，恩典就在哪裡格外增多。 The law came along to multiply the trespass. But where sin multiplied, grace multiplied even more,
21. 這樣，就像罪藉著死亡掌權，恩典也照樣藉著義掌權，使人藉著我們的主耶穌基督進入永恆的生命。 so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace will reign through righteousness, resulting in eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
Romans 6
1. 那麼，我們要怎麼說呢？難道我們可以留在罪中，好讓恩典增多嗎？ What should we say then? Should we continue in sin in order that grace may multiply?
2. 絕對不可！我們這些向罪已經死了的人，怎麼還能活在罪中呢？ Absolutely not! How can we who died to sin still live in it?
3. 難道你們不明白，所有受洗歸入基督耶穌的人，就是受洗歸入了他的死嗎？ Or are you unaware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?
4. 所以，我們藉著洗禮歸入死，和他一同埋葬，好使我們也能以生命的新樣式行事為人，就像基督藉著父的榮耀從死人中復活那樣。 Therefore we were buried with Him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too may walk in a new way of life.
5. 就是說，如果我們在基督死的樣式上與他聯合，也將要在他復活的形式上與他聯合。 For if we have been joined with Him in the likeness of His death, we will certainly also be in the likeness of His resurrection.
6. 我們知道，我們的舊我 已經和基督一起被釘十字架，好讓罪的身體被廢除，使我們不再做罪的奴僕， For we know that our old self was crucified with Him in order that sin's dominion over the body may be abolished, so that we may no longer be enslaved to sin,
7. 因為一個死了的人，已經脫離了罪。 since a person who has died is freed from sin's claims.
8. 那麼，如果我們與基督一同死了，就相信也要與他一同活著。 Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him,
9. 我們知道，基督既從死人中復活，就不會再死，死亡再也轄制不了他。 because we know that Christ, having been raised from the dead, no longer dies. Death no longer rules over Him.
10. 原來他死，是一次性地向罪而死；他活，是向神而活。 For in that He died, He died to sin once for all; but in that He lives, He lives to God.
11. 照樣，你們就當看自己向罪是死的，但在 基督耶穌裡向神卻是活的。 So, you too consider yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
12. 所以，不要讓罪在你們會死的身體上掌權，使你們順從身體的私欲； Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, so that you obey its desires.
13. 也不要把你們身體的任何部分 獻給罪，做不義的器具；相反，要像從死人中復活的人，把自己獻給神，並把身體的各部分做義的器具獻給神。 And do not offer any parts of it to sin as weapons for unrighteousness. But as those who are alive from the dead, offer yourselves to God, and all the parts of yourselves to God as weapons for righteousness.
14. 這樣，罪就不能轄制你們了，因為你們不在律法之下，而在恩典之下。 For sin will not rule over you, because you are not under law but under grace.
15. 那又怎麼樣呢？難道因為我們不在律法之下而在恩典之下，就可以犯罪嗎？絕對不可！ What then? Should we sin because we are not under law but under grace? Absolutely not!
16. 你們難道不知道嗎？你們把自己獻上做奴僕去順從誰，那麼，順從誰就是誰的奴僕：或做罪的奴僕，以至於死；或做順從的奴僕，以致稱義。 Do you not know that if you offer yourselves to someone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of that one you obey-- either of sin leading to death or of obedience leading to righteousness?
17. 感謝神！雖然你們過去是罪的奴僕，但現在卻從心裡順從了所傳給你們的 教導內容， But thank God that, although you used to be slaves of sin, you obeyed from the heart that pattern of teaching you were entrusted to,
18. 從罪中得了釋放，成為義的奴僕。 and having been liberated from sin, you became enslaved to righteousness.
19. 因著你們肉體的軟弱，我就按照人的說法來講，那就是，你們從前怎樣把身體的各部分 獻給汙穢和罪惡 做奴僕，以致罪惡 ；現在也要照樣把你們身體的各部分獻給義做奴僕，以致分別為聖。 I am using a human analogy because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you offered the parts of yourselves as slaves to moral impurity, and to greater and greater lawlessness, so now offer them as slaves to righteousness, which results in sanctification.
20. 原來，你們做罪的奴僕時，不受義的管束； For when you were slaves of sin, you were free from allegiance to righteousness.
21. 那麼，在你們現在看為羞恥的那些事上，你們當時到底得了什麼果子呢？那些事的結局就是死。 And what fruit was produced then from the things you are now ashamed of? For the end of those things is death.
22. 但如今，你們既從罪中得了釋放，成為神的奴僕，就得了果子，以致分別為聖，那結局就是永恆的生命。 But now, since you have been liberated from sin and become enslaved to God, you have your fruit, which results in sanctification-- and the end is eternal life!
23. 因為罪的工價就是死；但神的恩賜，在我們的主基督耶穌裡，卻是永恆的生命。 For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Romans 7
1. 弟兄們，我現在對明白律法的人說：難道你們不明白，律法只是在一個人活著的時候轄制這個人嗎？ Since I am speaking to those who understand law, brothers, are you unaware that the law has authority over someone as long as he lives?
2. 要知道，已婚的女人，在丈夫活著的時候，是被律法約束的；但如果丈夫死了，她就脫離了那關於丈夫的律法。 For example, a married woman is legally bound to her husband while he lives. But if her husband dies, she is released from the law regarding the husband.
3. 由此可見，丈夫還活著的時候，她如果歸向別的男人，就被稱為淫婦；但如果丈夫死了，她就脫離那律法得了自由，即使歸向別的男人，也不是淫婦。 So then, if she gives herself to another man while her husband is living, she will be called an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she is free from that law. Then, if she gives herself to another man, she is not an adulteress.
4. 因此，我的弟兄們，你們藉著基督的身體，在律法上也被處死了，使你們歸向另一位，就是從死人中復活的那一位，好讓我們能為神結出果子來。 Therefore, my brothers, you also were put to death in relation to the law through the [crucified] body of the Messiah, so that you may belong to another-- to Him who was raised from the dead-- that we may bear fruit for God.
5. 原來，當我們還在肉體中的時候，罪的欲望藉著律法在我們身體的各部分 做工，以致為死亡結了果子。 For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions operated through the law in every part of us and bore fruit for death.
6. 但如今，我們既然在那捆綁我們的律法上死了，就脫離了律法，結果我們得以按照聖靈的新樣式來服事，而不按照律法條文的舊樣式。 But now we have been released from the law, since we have died to what held us, so that we may serve in the new way of the Spirit and not in the old letter of the law.
7. 那麼，我們要怎麼說呢？難道律法是罪嗎？絕對不是！然而，要不是藉著律法，我就不知道什麼是罪。如果律法沒有說 「不可貪心」，我就不知道什麼是貪心； What should we say then? Is the law sin? Absolutely not! On the contrary, I would not have known sin if it were not for the law. For example, I would not have known what it is to covet if the law had not said, You shall not covet.
8. 但是，罪藉著誡命，趁機在我裡面生出種種貪念。原來在律法之外，罪是死的。 And sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, produced in me coveting of every kind. For apart from the law sin is dead.
9. 我從前活在律法之外，但是誡命一來，罪就活起來了， Once I was alive apart from the law, but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life
10. 我卻死了。於是我發現，那本該帶來生命的誡命，它卻導致了死亡。 and I died. The commandment that was meant for life resulted in death for me.
11. 事實上，罪藉著誡命趁機欺騙了我，並藉著誡命殺了我。 For sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.
12. 因此，律法是神聖的，誡命也是神聖、公義、美善的。 So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good.
13. 那麼，是那美善的導致了我的死嗎？ 絕對不是！而是罪。罪為要顯出是罪，就藉著那美善的帶來了我的死，使罪藉著誡命變得極其邪惡。 Therefore, did what is good cause my death? Absolutely not! On the contrary, sin, in order to be recognized as sin, was producing death in me through what is good, so that through the commandment sin might become sinful beyond measure.
14. 我們知道律法是屬靈的；而我是屬肉體的，已經賣給罪了。 For we know that the law is spiritual; but I am made out of flesh, sold into sin's power.
15. 實際上，我所做的，我不明白，因為我所願意的，我沒有去做；我所恨惡的，我反而去做。 For I do not understand what I am doing, because I do not practice what I want to do, but I do what I hate.
16. 那麼，如果我做我不願意做的事，我就贊同了律法是好的。 And if I do what I do not want to do, I agree with the law that it is good.
17. 所以現在這事就不再是我所做的，而是住在我裡面的罪所做的。 So now I am no longer the one doing it, but it is sin living in me.
18. 事實上，我知道在我裡面，就是在我肉體中，沒有良善；因為行善的意願在我裡面，卻行不出來。 For I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my flesh. For the desire to do what is good is with me, but there is no ability to do it.
19. 這樣，我願意行的善，我沒有去行；我不願意做的惡，我反而去做。 For I do not do the good that I want to do, but I practice the evil that I do not want to do.
20. 那麼，如果我做我不願意做的事，這事就不再是我所做的，而是住在我裡面的罪所做的。 Now if I do what I do not want, I am no longer the one doing it, but it is the sin that lives in me.
21. 因此我發現一個法則：當我願意行善的時候，惡就在我裡面。 So I discover this principle: when I want to do good, evil is with me.
22. 就是說，按著內在的人，我喜愛神的法則， For in my inner self I joyfully agree with God's law.
23. 然而我發現在我身體 中另有一個法則，與我理性的法則交戰，把我擄到我身體中罪的法則裡。 But I see a different law in the parts of my body, waging war against the law of my mind and taking me prisoner to the law of sin in the parts of my body.
24. 我這個人真是可悲呀！誰能救我脫離這屬於死亡的身體呢？ What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?
25. 藉著我們的主耶穌基督，感謝歸於神！ 由此可見，我自己一方面在理性上服從神的法則，另一方面在肉體中卻服從罪的法則。 I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, with my mind I myself am a slave to the law of God, but with my flesh, to the law of sin.
Romans 8
1. 所以現在，那些在基督耶穌裡的人， 就不被定罪了， Therefore, no condemnation now exists for those in Christ Jesus,
2. 因為聖靈的生命法則，在基督耶穌裡把你 從罪和死的法則中釋放了出來。 because the Spirit's law of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death.
3. 因肉體軟弱的緣故，律法所做不到的，神卻做到了 ——神派遣了自己的兒子成為罪的肉身樣式，並且為了贖罪，用肉身判決了罪， What the law could not do since it was limited by the flesh, God did. He condemned sin in the flesh by sending His own Son in flesh like ours under sin's domain, and as a sin offering,
4. 使律法的公義規定，成全在我們這些不順著肉體卻順著聖靈行走的人身上。 in order that the law's requirement would be accomplished in us who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.
5. 要知道，順著肉體的人，思想屬肉體的事；順著聖靈的人，思想屬聖靈的事。 For those whose lives are according to the flesh think about the things of the flesh, but those whose lives are according to the Spirit, about the things of the Spirit.
6. 屬肉體的思想帶來死亡；屬聖靈的思想帶來生命和平安。 For the mind-set of the flesh is death, but the mind-set of the Spirit is life and peace.
7. 原來屬肉體的思想是敵對神的，因為它不服從神的律法，其實也不能服從； For the mind-set of the flesh is hostile to God because it does not submit itself to God's law, for it is unable to do so.
8. 並且，屬肉體的人無法得到神的喜悅。 Those whose lives are in the flesh are unable to please God.
9. 但既然神的靈真是住在你們裡面，你們就不屬於肉體，而屬於聖靈了。不過如果有人沒有基督的靈，這個人就不屬於基督了。 You, however, are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, since the Spirit of God lives in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Him.
10. 但如果基督在你們裡面，那麼，你們的身體雖然因罪是死的，靈卻因義是活的 ； Now if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness.
11. 不但如此，使耶穌從死人中復活的那一位——他的靈如果住在你們裡面，那麼，使基督從死人中復活的那一位，也將藉著 住在你們裡面的聖靈，使你們會死的身體得著生命。 And if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead lives in you, then He who raised Christ from the dead will also bring your mortal bodies to life through His Spirit who lives in you.
12. 弟兄們，由此可見，我們都是有責任 的，但不是對肉體有責任去順著肉體而活； So then, brothers, we are not obligated to the flesh to live according to the flesh,
13. 因為你們如果順著肉體而活，就將死去；但如果順著聖靈治死身體的所作所為，就將活著。 for if you live according to the flesh, you are going to die. But if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
14. 原來，凡是蒙神的靈帶領的人，他們才是神的兒女。 All those led by God's Spirit are God's sons.
15. 就是說，你們所領受的不是一個奴役的靈，使你們再有懼怕；相反，你們所領受的是使你們有兒子名份的聖靈——藉著他，我們呼叫：「阿爸！父啊！」 For you did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry out, "Abba, Father!"
16. 聖靈親自與我們的靈一同作證：我們是神的兒女。 The Spirit Himself testifies together with our spirit that we are God's children,
17. 既然是兒女，也就是繼承人；如果我們真是為了與他一同得榮耀而與他一同受苦，我們就是神的繼承人，而且與基督同做繼承人。 and if children, also heirs-- heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ-- seeing that we suffer with Him so that we may also be glorified with Him.
18. 事實上，我認為現今時刻的苦難，與將來要顯明給我們的榮耀，是無法相比的。 For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is going to be revealed to us.
19. 被造之物都熱切盼望、熱切等待著神的兒女顯現出來， For the creation eagerly waits with anticipation for God's sons to be revealed.
20. 因為被造之物屈從在虛妄之下，並不是出於自願，而是出於使它屈從的那一位； For the creation was subjected to futility-- not willingly, but because of Him who subjected it-- in the hope
21. 被造之物自己也盼望著從使之衰朽 的奴役中得到釋放，歸入神兒女榮耀的自由。 that the creation itself will also be set free from the bondage of corruption into the glorious freedom of God's children.
22. 我們知道，所有被造之物都一同呻吟、同受陣痛，直到如今。 For we know that the whole creation has been groaning together with labor pains until now.
23. 不僅如此，連我們這些有聖靈為初熟果子的人，也在自己裡面呻吟嘆息，熱切等待得到兒子的名份，就是等待我們的身體得蒙救贖。 And not only that, but we ourselves who have the Spirit as the firstfruits-- we also groan within ourselves, eagerly waiting for adoption, the redemption of our bodies.
24. 因為我們得救在於這盼望。然而，看得見的盼望，就不是盼望了；誰會盼望自己所看得見的呢？ Now in this hope we were saved, yet hope that is seen is not hope, because who hopes for what he sees?
25. 但如果我們盼望那看不見的，就要藉著忍耐來熱切等待。 But if we hope for what we do not see, we eagerly wait for it with patience.
26. 況且，聖靈也照樣扶助我們的軟弱。事實上，我們不知道該禱告什麼、如何禱告，但聖靈卻親自用說不出的嘆息，為我們 代求。 In the same way the Spirit also joins to help in our weakness, because we do not know what to pray for as we should, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with unspoken groanings.
27. 而且，洞察人心的那一位，知道聖靈的意念是什麼，因為聖靈是按神的意思 為聖徒代求的。 And He who searches the hearts knows the Spirit's mind-set, because He intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.
28. 我們也知道，神使萬事相輔相成，是為了愛神之人的益處，就是那些按照他的心意蒙召之人的益處。 We know that all things work together for the good of those who love God: those who are called according to His purpose.
29. 因為神預先所知道的人，神也預先定下他們和他兒子的形像相似，使他兒子在眾多弟兄中做長子 ； For those He foreknew He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers.
30. 而且，神預先所定下的人，神又召他們來；所召來的人，又稱他們為義；所稱為義的人，又使他們得榮耀。 And those He predestined, He also called; and those He called, He also justified; and those He justified, He also glorified.
31. 那麼，對這些事我們要怎麼說呢？ 神如果支持我們，誰還能反對我們呢？ What then are we to say about these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
32. 神既然沒有顧惜自己的兒子， 為我們所有的人捨棄了他， 難道不會把萬有也連同他一起賜給我們嗎？ He did not even spare His own Son, but offered Him up for us all; how will He not also with Him grant us everything?
33. 到底誰能控告那些蒙神揀選的人呢？ 神是稱人為義的那一位！ Who can bring an accusation against God's elect? God is the One who justifies.
34. 到底誰能定我們的罪呢？ 基督耶穌是已經死了的那一位—— 但更要說，他已經復活了， 而且現今在神的右邊，還為我們代求！ Who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus is the One who died, but even more, has been raised; He also is at the right hand of God and intercedes for us.
35. 到底誰能使我們與基督 的愛分開呢？ 難道是患難嗎？是困苦嗎？是逼迫嗎？ 是飢餓嗎？是赤身嗎？是危險嗎？是刀劍嗎？ Who can separate us from the love of Christ? Can affliction or anguish or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?
36. 正如經上所記： 「為你的緣故，我們終日被置於死地， 被看為要宰殺的羊。」 As it is written: Because of You we are being put to death all day long; we are counted as sheep to be slaughtered.
37. 然而，靠著愛我們的那一位， 我們在這一切事上已經得勝有餘了。 No, in all these things we are more than victorious through Him who loved us.
38. 事實上，我深信： 無論是死、是生、 是天使、是統治者、 是現在的事、是將來的事、是有勢力的、 For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor rulers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
39. 是高處的、是深處的，或是任何別的被造之物， 都不能使我們與神的愛分開， 這愛是在我們主基督耶穌裡的。 nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will have the power to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord!
Romans 9
1. 我在基督裡說真話，不是在說謊；我的良心藉著聖靈與我一同作證： I speak the truth in Christ-- I am not lying; my conscience is testifying to me with the Holy Spirit--
2. 我極其憂傷，心裡時常苦痛。 that I have intense sorrow and continual anguish in my heart.
3. 為了我的同胞，我的骨肉之親，就算我自己被詛咒、與基督分離，我也願意。 For I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from the Messiah for the benefit of my brothers, my countrymen by physical descent.
4. 他們是 以色列 人：兒子的名份、榮耀、諸約、所賜的律法、禮儀、各樣應許，都是他們的； They are Israelites, and to them belong the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the temple service, and the promises.
5. 祖先也是他們的；照著肉身說，基督也是出自他們的——他是那在萬有之上當受頌讚的神，直到永遠！阿們。 The forefathers are theirs, and from them, by physical descent, came the Messiah, who is God over all, blessed forever. Amen.
6. 但這並不是說神的話語 落了空，因為由 以色列 所生的，並不都是 以色列 人； But it is not as though the word of God has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.
7. 也不因為是 亞伯拉罕 的後裔，就都是他的兒女；只有 「從 以撒 生的，才會被稱為你的後裔。」 Neither are they all children because they are Abraham's descendants. On the contrary, in Isaac your seed will be called.
8. 這就是說，肉身的兒女並不是神的兒女，只有應許的兒女才算是後裔。 That is, it is not the children by physical descent who are God's children, but the children of the promise are considered seed.
9. 原來所應許的話是這樣的： 「到明年 這時候我要來， 撒拉 會生一個兒子。」 For this is the statement of the promise: At this time I will come, and Sarah will have a son.
10. 不僅如此， 麗貝卡 也是這樣。她由一個人，就是由我們的先祖 以撒 懷了孕。 And not only that, but also when Rebekah became pregnant by Isaac our forefather
11. 實際上，雙子 還沒有出生，也沒有行善或作惡以前——為了要顯明神的揀選心意不是本於人的行為，而是出於召喚人的那一位—— (for though they had not been born yet or done anything good or bad, so that God's purpose according to election might stand,
12. 神 就對 麗貝卡 說： 「大的將要服事小的。」 not from works but from the One who calls) she was told: The older will serve the younger.
13. 正如經上所記： 「我愛 雅各，卻恨 以掃 。」 As it is written: Jacob I have loved, but Esau I have hated.
14. 那麼，我們要怎麼說呢？難道神不公義嗎？絕對不是！ What should we say then? Is there injustice with God? Absolutely not!
15. 因為神對 摩西 說： 「我要憐憫誰，就憐憫誰； 我要同情誰，就同情誰。」 For He tells Moses: I will show mercy to whom I show mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.
16. 由此可見，這不在於人的意願，也不在於人的努力，而在於施憐憫的神。 So then it does not depend on human will or effort, but on God who shows mercy.
17. 原來經上有話對法老說： 「我興起你，正是為此： 好讓我藉著你來顯出我的大能， 使我的名傳遍天下。」 For the Scripture tells Pharaoh: For this reason I raised you up: so that I may display My power in you, and that My name may be proclaimed in all the earth.
18. 這樣看來，神要憐憫誰，就憐憫誰；要使誰頑固，就使誰頑固。 So then, He shows mercy to whom He wills, and He hardens whom He wills.
19. 那麼，你會對我說：「既然如此，神為什麼還要指責人呢？到底誰能抵擋他的旨意呢？」 You will say to me, therefore, "Why then does He still find fault? For who can resist His will?"
20. 哦，人哪！你到底是誰，竟然向神頂嘴呢？被造的難道可以對造它的說：「你為什麼把我造成這樣呢？」 But who are you-- anyone who talks back to God? Will what is formed say to the one who formed it, "Why did you make me like this?"
21. 難道陶匠沒有權柄從同一團泥中，既造出貴重的器皿，又造出卑賤的器皿嗎？ Or has the potter no right over His clay, to make from the same lump one piece of pottery for honor and another for dishonor?
22. 但如果神想要顯出他的震怒，顯明他的能力，就以極大的耐心容忍那些承受震怒的器皿，就是他早已預備要歸於滅亡 的器皿，那又怎麼樣呢？ And what if God, desiring to display His wrath and to make His power known, endured with much patience objects of wrath ready for destruction?
23. 再者，如果這是為要將他那榮耀的豐盛顯明在這些得蒙憐憫的器皿，就是他早已預備要歸於榮耀的器皿上，那又怎麼樣呢？ And [what if] He did this to make known the riches of His glory on objects of mercy that He prepared beforehand for glory--
24. 這些器皿就是我們這些蒙召的人：不僅是從 猶太 人中，也是從外邦人中蒙召的人。 on us whom He also called, not only from the Jews but also from the Gentiles?
25. 正如神在 何西阿 書上也說： 「我將要稱那不是我子民的為『我的子民』， 那不蒙愛的為『蒙愛的』。 As He also says in Hosea: I will call "Not-My-People," "My-People," and she who is "Unloved," "Beloved."
26. 從前在什麼地方對他們說 『你們不是我的子民』， 就在那裡，他們將被稱為『永生神的兒女。』 」 And it will be in the place where they were told, you are not My people, there they will be called sons of the living God.
27. 以賽亞 論到 以色列 人，呼喊說： 「 子民的人數雖然多如海沙， 將要得救的卻是剩餘的少數。 But Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: Though the number of Israel's sons is like the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved;
28. 主就是要在地上 徹底、迅速地成就他的話。」 for the Lord will execute His sentence completely and decisively on the earth.
29. 又如 以賽亞 預先說過： 「要不是萬軍之主給我們留下後裔， 我們早就變得像 所多瑪 、 格摩拉 那樣了。」 And just as Isaiah predicted: If the Lord of Hosts had not left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom, and we would have been made like Gomorrah.
30. 那麼，我們要怎麼說呢？那原來沒有追求義的外邦人，卻得到了義，就是因信而得的義； What should we say then? Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained righteousness-- namely the righteousness that comes from faith.
31. 而 以色列 人追求律法的義，卻沒有達到律法的義 。 But Israel, pursuing the law for righteousness, has not achieved the law.
32. 這是為什麼呢？因為他們不是本於信，倒像是本於 行為去追求的，所以他們就絆倒在那「絆腳的石頭」上。 Why is that? Because they did not pursue it by faith, but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone.
33. 正如經上所記： 「看哪，我在 錫安 放一塊絆腳的石頭， 是使人絆倒的磐石； 可是信靠他的人將不至於蒙羞。」 As it is written: Look! I am putting a stone in Zion to stumble over, and a rock to trip over, yet the one who believes on Him will not be put to shame.
Romans 10
1. 弟兄們，我心裡熱切盼望，並替 以色列 人 向神祈求，是為了他們的救恩。 Brothers, my heart's desire and prayer to God concerning them is for their salvation!
2. 我見證他們對神有熱心，但不是按著真正的認識。 I can testify about them that they have zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.
3. 就是說，他們不明白神的義，想要確立自己的義，就不服從神的義了。 Because they disregarded the righteousness from God and attempted to establish their own righteousness, they have not submitted to God's righteousness.
4. 事實上，基督是律法的終結，使所有相信的人都以致稱義。 For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.
5. 原來，有關出於律法的義， 摩西 寫道： 「遵行這些事的人，將因此而活」 ； For Moses writes about the righteousness that is from the law: The one who does these things will live by them.
6. 而有關本於信的義，卻這樣吩咐： 「你心裡不用說：誰要升到天上去？」 ——這意思是要把基督帶下來； But the righteousness that comes from faith speaks like this: Do not say in your heart, "Who will go up to heaven?" that is, to bring Christ down
7. 「也不用說： 誰要下到無底坑去 ？ 」——這意思是將基督從死人中領上來。 or, "Who will go down into the abyss?" that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.
8. 然而，這是怎麼說呢？ 「這話就在你身邊，在你口中，在你心裡。」 這就是我們所傳的有關信仰的話語： On the contrary, what does it say? The message is near you, in your mouth and in your heart. This is the message of faith that we proclaim:
9. 你如果口裡承認耶穌是主，心裡相信神使他從死人中復活，就將得救。 if you confess with your mouth, "Jesus is Lord," and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.
10. 就是說，人心裡相信以致稱義，口裡承認以致救恩， With the heart one believes, resulting in righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses, resulting in salvation.
11. 因為經上說： 「所有信靠他的人將不至於蒙羞。」 Now the Scripture says, No one who believes on Him will be put to shame,
12. 猶太 人和外邦人 並沒有分別，原來，萬人共同的主，使所有求告他的人都富足。 for there is no distinction between Jew and Greek, since the same Lord of all is rich to all who call on Him.
13. 的確， 「無論誰求告主名，都將得救。」 For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.
14. 既然如此，人沒有相信他，怎麼能求告他呢？沒有聽說過他，怎麼能相信他呢？沒有人傳講，怎麼能聽到呢？ But how can they call on Him in whom they have not believed? And how can they believe without hearing about Him? And how can they hear without a preacher?
15. 如果沒有奉差派，又怎麼能去傳講呢？正如經上所記： 「 傳講美好福音的人，他們的腳蹤多麼美麗！」 And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: How welcome are the feet of those who announce the gospel of good things!
16. 但是，並不是所有的人都順從了福音，就如 以賽亞 所說： 「主啊，我們所傳的，有誰信了呢？」 But all did not obey the gospel. For Isaiah says, Lord, who has believed our message?
17. 因此，信是由聽而來，聽是藉著基督 的話而來。 So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the message about Christ.
18. 那麼我要說，他們難道沒有聽過嗎？當然聽過—— 「那聲音傳遍了天下， 那話語傳到了地極。」 But I ask, "Did they not hear?" Yes, they did: Their voice has gone out to all the earth, and their words to the ends of the inhabited world.
19. 我再說「 以色列 人難道不明白嗎？」首先， 摩西 說： 「我要用不是子民的，激起你們的嫉妒之心， 用無知的民族激起你們的怒氣。」 But I ask, "Did Israel not understand?" First, Moses said: I will make you jealous of those who are not a nation; I will make you angry by a nation that lacks understanding.
20. 後來， 以賽亞 大膽地說： 「沒有尋找我的，我讓他們尋見； 沒有求問我的，我向他們顯現。」 And Isaiah says boldly: I was found by those who were not looking for Me; I revealed Myself to those who were not asking for Me.
21. 但是關於 以色列 人，他卻說： 「我整天向那悖逆、頂嘴的子民伸出雙手。」 But to Israel he says: All day long I have spread out My hands to a disobedient and defiant people.
Romans 11
1. 那麼，我要問，難道神棄絕了他的子民嗎？絕對沒有！其實我也是 以色列 人， 亞伯拉罕 的後裔，屬於 便雅憫 支派。 I ask, then, has God rejected His people? Absolutely not! For I too am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.
2. 神並沒有棄絕自己預先所知道的子民。難道你們不知道那有關 以利亞 的經文怎麼說嗎？他怎樣向神抱怨 以色列 人呢？ God has not rejected His people whom He foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says in the Elijah section-- how he pleads with God against Israel?
3. 「主啊，他們殺了你的先知們，拆毀了你的祭壇， 只剩下我一個人，他們還要追索我的命。」 Lord, they have killed Your prophets, torn down Your altars; and I am the only one left, and they are trying to take my life!
4. 但神對他的答覆是怎麼說的呢？ 「我為自己保留了七千人，他們是沒有向 巴力 屈膝的。」 But what was God's reply to him? I have left 7,000 men for Myself who have not bowed down to Baal.
5. 照樣，在現今的時刻也有剩餘的少數，就是藉著恩典蒙揀選的人。 In the same way, then, there is also at the present time a remnant chosen by grace.
6. 既然藉著恩典，就不再本於行為了；否則，恩典就不再是恩典了。 Now if by grace, then it is not by works; otherwise grace ceases to be grace.
7. 所以怎麼樣呢？ 以色列 人並沒有獲得他們所尋求的，蒙揀選的人卻獲得了，而其餘的人都成了剛硬的， What then? Israel did not find what it was looking for, but the elect did find it. The rest were hardened,
8. 正如經上所記： 「神給了他們昏迷的心靈、 看不見的眼睛、聽不見的耳朵， 直到今天。」 as it is written: God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that cannot see and ears that cannot hear, to this day.
9. 大衛 也說： 「讓他們的筵席成為網羅、陷阱、絆腳石， 又成為他們的報應。 And David says: Let their feasting become a snare and a trap, a pitfall and a retribution to them.
10. 讓他們的眼睛昏暗不能看。 讓他們的腰背永遠彎曲。」 Let their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent continually.
11. 所以我要問，難道 以色列 人跌倒了，是要他們敗落嗎？絕對不是！相反，因他們的過犯，救恩就臨到了外邦人，為要激起 以色列 人的嫉妒之心。 I ask, then, have they stumbled so as to fall? Absolutely not! On the contrary, by their stumbling, salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel jealous.
12. 既然他們的過犯能使世人富足，他們的失敗能使外邦人富足，更何況他們的全數滿足呢！ Now if their stumbling brings riches for the world, and their failure riches for the Gentiles, how much more will their full number bring!
13. 現在我向你們外邦人說話：既然我確實是外邦人的使徒，我就以我的服事工作為榮耀， Now I am speaking to you Gentiles. In view of the fact that I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry,
14. 或許激起我同胞 的嫉妒之心，好拯救他們中的一些人。 if I can somehow make my own people jealous and save some of them.
15. 實際上，如果他們被丟棄，使世人與神 和好了，那麼他們蒙接納，如果不是從死人中復生，又是什麼呢？ For if their being rejected is world reconciliation, what will their acceptance mean but life from the dead?
16. 如果初熟的麥子 是聖潔的，那麵團也就聖潔了；如果樹根是聖潔的，那樹枝也就聖潔了。 Now if the firstfruits offered up are holy, so is the whole batch. And if the root is holy, so are the branches.
17. 但如果有些樹枝被折下來，而你這野橄欖枝被接在其上，並且一同有份於那橄欖樹根的豐富養分， Now if some of the branches were broken off, and you, though a wild olive branch, were grafted in among them, and have come to share in the rich root of the cultivated olive tree,
18. 那麼你就不應該向那些樹枝自誇了。而就算你自誇，也不是你托著樹根，而是樹根托著你。 do not brag that you are better than those branches. But if you do brag-- you do not sustain the root, but the root sustains you.
19. 這樣，你會說：「那些樹枝被折下來，就是要我能被接上去。」 Then you will say, "Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in."
20. 不錯！他們因不信被折了下來，而你因信已經站立得住；你不可心高氣傲，反要懼怕； True enough; they were broken off by unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be arrogant, but be afraid.
21. 因為神如果沒有顧惜原生的樹枝，恐怕也不會顧惜你。 For if God did not spare the natural branches, He will not spare you either.
22. 所以看哪！神的仁慈和嚴厲——對墮落的人，神一定是嚴厲的，但是對你，如果你留在他的仁慈中，神就是仁慈的；否則，你也將被砍下來。 Therefore, consider God's kindness and severity: severity toward those who have fallen, but God's kindness toward you-- if you remain in His kindness. Otherwise you too will be cut off.
23. 而且，那些被折下來的樹枝 如果不再堅持不信，也將被接上，因為神能夠把他們重新接上。 And even they, if they do not remain in unbelief, will be grafted in, because God has the power to graft them in again.
24. 要知道，如果你從天然的野橄欖樹上被砍下來，尚且能違反自然、被接在栽培的橄欖樹上，何況那些原生的樹枝，難道不更能接在自己的橄欖樹上嗎？ For if you were cut off from your native wild olive, and against nature were grafted into a cultivated olive tree, how much more will these-- the natural branches-- be grafted into their own olive tree?
25. 弟兄們，我不願意你們不明白這奧祕，免得你們自以為聰明。這奧祕就是： 以色列 人中的部分人變得剛硬，直到外邦人的全數滿足了， So that you will not be conceited, brothers, I do not want you to be unaware of this mystery: a partial hardening has come to Israel until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.
26. 以色列 全家才會得救，正如經上所記： 「一位拯救者將從 錫安 而來， 他要從 雅各 除去不敬神的心， And in this way all Israel will be saved, as it is written: The Liberator will come from Zion; He will turn away godlessness from Jacob.
27. 這就是我的約—— 當我除去他們罪孽的時候，所給他們的約。」 And this will be My covenant with them, when I take away their sins.
28. 就福音而言，他們因你們的緣故，固然是神的 敵人 ；但就揀選而言，他們因祖先的緣故，卻是蒙愛的， Regarding the gospel, they are enemies for your advantage, but regarding election, they are loved because of their forefathers,
29. 因為神的恩賜和召喚是不撤回的 。 since God's gracious gifts and calling are irrevocable.
30. 正如你們以前不肯信從神而現在卻因他們的不信從反而蒙了憐憫； As you once disobeyed God, but now have received mercy through their disobedience,
31. 照樣，他們如今也不肯信從，為要藉著你們所蒙的憐憫，讓他們現在 也可以蒙憐憫， so they too have now disobeyed, [resulting] in mercy to you, so that they also now may receive mercy.
32. 因為神把所有的人都圈在不信從之中，是為了要憐憫所有的人。 For God has imprisoned all in disobedience, so that He may have mercy on all.
33. 哦，深奧啊！神的智慧和知識的財富！ 他的判斷是多麼地無法探究， 他的道 是多麼地無法測度！ Oh, the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable His judgments and untraceable His ways!
34. 「到底是誰知道主的心意？ 是誰做過他的謀士？ For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?
35. 又是誰首先給了主， 使自己將來得到回報呢？ 」 Or who has ever first given to Him, and has to be repaid?
36. 因為萬有都是出於他、藉著他、歸於他。 願榮耀歸於他，直到永遠！阿們。 For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever. Amen.
Romans 12
1. 所以弟兄們，我藉著神的各樣憐憫勸你們，要把自己的身體獻上，做為聖潔、蒙神喜悅的活祭；這是你們理所當然的 事奉。 Therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, I urge you to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God; this is your spiritual worship.
2. 不要效法這世代，要藉著理性的更新而改變，使你們可以分辨什麼是神的旨意——那美善、可喜悅、完美的旨意。 Do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may discern what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.
3. 我藉著所賜給我的恩典，對你們中間的每個人說：不要自視過高，過於所當看的，而要照著神所分給每個人信心的尺度，清醒地看自己。 For by the grace given to me, I tell everyone among you not to think of himself more highly than he should think. Instead, think sensibly, as God has distributed a measure of faith to each one.
4. 正如我們一個身體有很多部分，而且各部分都有不同的功用； Now as we have many parts in one body, and all the parts do not have the same function,
5. 照樣，我們這許多人，在基督裡是一個身體，而且各個部分都彼此相屬。 in the same way we who are many are one body in Christ and individually members of one another.
6. 照著所賜給我們的恩典，我們各有不同的恩賜： 如果是做先知傳道 的恩賜，就按照信心的程度用它 ； According to the grace given to us, we have different gifts: If prophecy, use it according to the standard of faith;
7. 如果是服事的，就用在服事上； 如果是教導的，就用在教導上； if service, in service; if teaching, in teaching;
8. 如果是勸勉的，就用在勸勉上； 分享的，要慷慨； 帶領 的，要殷勤； 憐憫人的，要甘心樂意。 if exhorting, in exhortation; giving, with generosity; leading, with diligence; showing mercy, with cheerfulness.
9. 愛，不要虛假；要厭棄惡、持守善； Love must be without hypocrisy. Detest evil; cling to what is good.
10. 要以弟兄之情彼此相愛，以尊敬之心彼此謙讓， Show family affection to one another with brotherly love. Outdo one another in showing honor.
11. 殷勤而不懶惰，靈裡時時火熱，常常服事主。 Do not lack diligence; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord.
12. 在盼望中要歡喜，在患難裡要忍耐，在禱告上要恆切。 Rejoice in hope; be patient in affliction; be persistent in prayer.
13. 要分擔聖徒的缺乏；盡力款待客旅。 Share with the saints in their needs; pursue hospitality.
14. 要祝福那些逼迫你們的人；要祝福，不要詛咒。 Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse.
15. 要與快樂的人一同快樂；與哀哭的人一同哀哭。 Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
16. 要彼此同心；不要心高氣傲，而要俯就卑微 的人；不要自以為聰明。 Be in agreement with one another. Do not be proud; instead, associate with the humble. Do not be wise in your own estimation.
17. 不要對任何人以惡報惡；要敬重所有的人看為美善的事； Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Try to do what is honorable in everyone's eyes.
18. 如果有可能，盡量在你們的事上與所有的人和睦。 If possible, on your part, live at peace with everyone.
19. 各位蒙愛的人哪，不要自己報復，寧可給神的震怒留地步，因為經上記著： 「主說：報應在我，我將回報。」 Friends, do not avenge yourselves; instead, leave room for His wrath. For it is written: Vengeance belongs to Me; I will repay, says the Lord.
20. 不但如此， 「如果你的敵人 餓了，就給他吃； 如果他渴了，就給他喝； 因為你這樣做，就是把炭火堆在他的頭上。」 But If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him something to drink. For in so doing you will be heaping fiery coals on his head.
21. 不要被惡所勝，反要以善勝惡。 Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.
Romans 13
1. 所有的人 都當服從在上掌權的，因為沒有一個掌權的不是出於神。所有掌權的，都是由神所指定的。 Everyone must submit to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and those that exist are instituted by God.
2. 所以，抗拒掌權的，就是違抗神所設立的；違抗的人，就自招懲罰。 So then, the one who resists the authority is opposing God's command, and those who oppose it will bring judgment on themselves.
3. 事實上，對良善的行為，掌權者並不是可怕的；而對邪惡的行為，他才是可怕的。那麼，你想要不懼怕掌權的，就應當做良善的事。這樣，你就會得到他的稱讚。 For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the authority? Do good and you will have its approval.
4. 要知道，他是神的僕役，對你是有益處的。但你如果作惡，就該懼怕，因為他不是毫無理由的佩帶刀劍。他是神的僕役，是報應者，使震怒臨到作惡的人。 For government is God's servant to you for good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, because it does not carry the sword for no reason. For government is God's servant, an avenger that brings wrath on the one who does wrong.
5. 因此，你們必須服從，不僅是為了震怒的緣故，也是為了良心。 Therefore, you must submit, not only because of wrath, but also because of your conscience.
6. 其實你們納稅，也是為了這緣故；因為他們是神的僕役，正是為此專心服事。 And for this reason you pay taxes, since the [authorities] are God's public servants, continually attending to these tasks.
7. 每個人所當得的，你們都要給他：當得稅的，就給他稅；當得捐的，就給他捐；當受敬畏的，就敬畏他；當受尊敬的，就尊敬他。 Pay your obligations to everyone: taxes to those you owe taxes, tolls to those you owe tolls, respect to those you owe respect, and honor to those you owe honor.
8. 你們對任何人都不要虧欠什麼；唯有在彼此相愛的事上，要常以為虧欠。實際上，愛別人的，就成全了律法。 Do not owe anyone anything, except to love one another, for the one who loves another has fulfilled the law.
9. 這是因為，那 「不可通姦，不可殺人，不可偷竊， 不可貪心」 的誡命，或是別的什麼誡命，都包含在 「要愛鄰如己」 這一句話裡了。 The commandments: You shall not commit adultery, you shall not murder, you shall not steal, you shall not covet, and if there is any other commandment-- all are summed up by this: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
10. 愛是對鄰人不做惡事，因此愛是成全律法的。 Love does no wrong to a neighbor. Love, therefore, is the fulfillment of the law.
11. 再者，你們已經看見了這個時代，是你們 早應該從沉睡中醒過來的時候，因為比我們初信的時候，我們的救恩現在更近了。 Besides this, knowing the time, it is already the hour for you to wake up from sleep, for now our salvation is nearer than when we first believed.
12. 黑夜已深，白晝近了。所以，我們要脫去黑暗的行為，配上光明的兵器。 The night is nearly over, and the daylight is near, so let us discard the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.
13. 我們要行事端正，好像在白晝中那樣：不可荒宴、醉酒；不可淫亂、好色；不可紛爭、嫉妒。 Let us walk with decency, as in the daylight: not in carousing and drunkenness; not in sexual impurity and promiscuity; not in quarreling and jealousy.
14. 相反，要穿上主耶穌基督；不要為了私欲而在屬肉體的事上做任何安排。 But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no plans to satisfy the fleshly desires.
Romans 14
1. 你們要接納在信仰上軟弱的人，避免在有爭議 的事上辯論。 Accept anyone who is weak in faith, but don't argue about doubtful issues.
2. 雖然有的人相信什麼都可以吃，但那軟弱的人卻只吃蔬菜。 One person believes he may eat anything, but one who is weak eats only vegetables.
3. 吃的人不要藐視不吃的人，不吃的人也不要評斷吃的人，因為神已經接納他了。 One who eats must not look down on one who does not eat; and one who does not eat must not criticize one who does, because God has accepted him.
4. 你到底是誰，竟然評斷別人的僕人？他或站穩或跌倒，是他自己主人的事；而且他會站得住，因為主 能使他站得住。 Who are you to criticize another's household slave? Before his own Lord he stands or falls. And stand he will! For the Lord is able to make him stand.
5. 雖然有的人判定這一天比那一天重要，但有的人卻判定每一天都一樣。每個人當在自己理性上確信不疑。 One person considers one day to be above another day. Someone else considers every day to be the same. Each one must be fully convinced in his own mind.
6. 注重某一天的人，是為主而注重的； 吃的人，是為主而吃的，因為他感謝神；不吃的人，也是為主不吃的，他也感謝神。 Whoever observes the day, observes it to the Lord. Whoever eats, eats to the Lord, since he gives thanks to God; and whoever does not eat, it is to the Lord that he does not eat, yet he thanks God.
7. 我們沒有一個人是為自己而活，也沒有一個人是為自己而死。 For none of us lives to himself, and no one dies to himself.
8. 就是說，我們如果活著，是為主而活；如果死了，是為主而死。所以，我們無論是活著，還是死了，總是屬於主。 If we live, we live to the Lord; and if we die, we die to the Lord. Therefore, whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
9. 正是為此，基督死了，而且復活了，要做死人和活人的主。 Christ died and came to life for this: that He might rule over both the dead and the living.
10. 至於你，為什麼評斷你的弟兄呢？又為什麼藐視你的弟兄呢？要知道，我們都要站在神 的審判臺前， But you, why do you criticize your brother? Or you, why do you look down on your brother? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of God.
11. 因為經上記著： 「主說：我指著我的永生起誓， 萬膝將向我跪下， 萬口將承認神。」 For it is written: As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow to Me, and every tongue will give praise to God.
12. 由此可見，我們每個人都要把自己的事向神做出交代。 So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.
13. 所以，我們不要再彼此評斷，倒要下定決心，不給弟兄放下絆跌物或絆腳石。 Therefore, let us no longer criticize one another, but instead decide not to put a stumbling block or pitfall in your brother's way.
14. 我知道，並且在主耶穌裡深信：沒有一樣東西本身是不潔淨的。只是，如果有人認為什麼是不潔淨的，對他來說，那就是不潔淨的。 (I know and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. Still, to someone who considers a thing to be unclean, to that one it is unclean.)
15. 如果因食物的緣故使你的弟兄憂傷，你就不再是憑著愛行事了。基督已經替他死了，不可因你的食物毀了他。 For if your brother is hurt by what you eat, you are no longer walking according to love. By what you eat, do not destroy that one for whom Christ died.
16. 所以，不要讓你們看為好的事受到毀謗， Therefore, do not let your good be slandered,
17. 因為神的國不在於吃喝，而在於聖靈裡的公義、和睦 、喜樂。 for the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
18. 要知道，如此服事基督的人，是蒙神喜悅的，也是受人讚許的。 Whoever serves the Messiah in this way is acceptable to God and approved by men.
19. 這樣看來，我們要追求和睦 的事和彼此造就的事。 So then, we must pursue what promotes peace and what builds up one another.
20. 不要因食物的緣故破壞神的工作。一切固然都是潔淨的，但如果有人因吃東西使人絆腳，這就是惡事了。 Do not tear down God's work because of food. Everything is clean, but it is wrong for a man to cause stumbling by what he eats.
21. 不在吃肉、喝酒、或其他事上使你的弟兄絆倒， 這才是好的。 It is a noble thing not to eat meat, or drink wine, or do anything that makes your brother stumble.
22. 你所持有的信念，自己要在神面前持有；在自己認為對的事上不自責的人是蒙福的。 Do you have faith? Keep it to yourself before God. Blessed is the man who does not condemn himself by what he approves.
23. 但那疑惑的人如果吃了，就被定罪了，因為不是本於信；而一切不是本於信的，就是罪。 But whoever doubts stands condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith, and everything that is not from faith is sin.
Romans 15
1. 我們堅強的人，應該擔當不堅強人的軟弱，不求自己的喜悅。 Now we who are strong have an obligation to bear the weaknesses of those without strength, and not to please ourselves.
2. 我們每個人當為了鄰人的益處讓他喜悅，使他得造就。 Each one of us must please his neighbor for his good, in order to build him up.
3. 因為基督不但不求自己的喜悅，反而像經上所記的： 「那些責罵你之人的責罵，都落在我身上了。」 For even the Messiah did not please Himself. On the contrary, as it is written, The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.
4. 實際上，凡是先前被記載的，都是為了教導我們而寫的，好讓我們藉著忍耐和經上的安慰，懷有盼望。 For whatever was written before was written for our instruction, so that through our endurance and through the encouragement of the Scriptures we may have hope.
5. 願賜忍耐和安慰的神，使你們藉著基督耶穌，彼此同心合意， Now may the God of endurance and encouragement grant you agreement with one another, according to Christ Jesus,
6. 好使你們同心同聲榮耀神——我們主耶穌基督的父。 so that you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ with a united mind and voice.
7. 因此，你們當彼此接納，就像基督也接納了你們 歸於神的榮耀。 Therefore accept one another, just as the Messiah also accepted you, to the glory of God.
8. 我是說：基督 為了神的真理，已成為受割禮之人 的僕人，為要證實對祖先的各樣應許， Now I say that Christ has become a servant of the circumcised on behalf of the truth of God, to confirm the promises to the fathers,
9. 並且使外邦人因著所蒙的憐憫而榮耀神，正如經上所記： 「為此，我要在外邦人中承認你， 歌頌你的名。」 and so that Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written: Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles, and I will sing psalms to Your name.
10. 經上又說： 「外邦人哪，你們要與他的子民一同慶祝！」 Again it says: Rejoice, you Gentiles, with His people!
11. 又說： 「萬國啊，你們要讚美主！ 萬民哪，你們要頌讚他！」 And again: Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles; all the peoples should praise Him!
12. 又有 以賽亞 說： 「將有 耶西 的根， 就是興起來統治外邦人的那一位； 外邦人要仰望他。」 And again, Isaiah says: The root of Jesse will appear, the One who rises to rule the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will hope.
13. 願賜盼望的神，因著你們的信，將一切喜樂和平安充滿你們，使你們藉著聖靈的能力滿懷盼望。 Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
14. 我的弟兄們，至於你們，我自己同樣深信：你們也滿有良善，充滿一切知識，又能彼此勸誡。 Now, my brothers, I myself am convinced about you that you also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and able to instruct one another.
15. 不過 我要提醒你們，藉著神所賜給我的恩典，我在部分地方寫得比較大膽。 Nevertheless, to remind you, I have written to you more boldly on some points because of the grace given me by God
16. 這恩典使我為外邦人成了基督耶穌的僕役、做了神福音的祭司，好讓外邦人藉著聖靈被分別為聖，成為蒙悅納的供物。 to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving as a priest of God's good news. My purpose is that the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
17. 所以，我在基督耶穌裡，在屬神的事上有可誇耀的。 Therefore I have reason to boast in Christ Jesus regarding what pertains to God.
18. 我什麼都不敢說，只說基督藉著我所完成的事，就是為了外邦人的順從，他藉著我所說的和所做的事， For I would not dare say anything except what Christ has accomplished through me to make the Gentiles obedient by word and deed,
19. 藉著神蹟、奇事的能力和聖靈 的能力所完成的事。結果我從 耶路撒冷 及其周圍一帶直到 伊利里亞，把基督的福音都傳遍了。 by the power of miraculous signs and wonders, and by the power of God's Spirit. As a result, I have fully proclaimed the good news about the Messiah from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum.
20. 這樣，我立定心志要在基督的名沒有被傳過的地方傳福音，免得建造在別人的根基上， So my aim is to evangelize where Christ has not been named, in order that I will not be building on someone else's foundation,
21. 正如經上所記： 「沒有聽說過他的人，將要看見； 沒有聽見過的人，將要領悟。」 but, as it is written: Those who had no report of Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.
22. 所以，我也多次受到攔阻，不能到你們那裡去。 That is why I have been prevented many times from coming to you.
23. 但如今，這些地區再沒有可傳的 地方了，況且多年來我一直渴望見到你們。 But now I no longer have any work to do in these provinces, and I have strongly desired for many years to come to you
24. 就是說，當我去 西班牙 的時候， 我希望能順路看你們；先與你們相聚，使我稍得滿足；然後由你們在那裡送我上路。 whenever I travel to Spain. For I do hope to see you when I pass through, and to be sent on my way there by you, once I have first enjoyed your company for a while.
25. 但如今，我要到 耶路撒冷 去服事聖徒， Now, however, I am traveling to Jerusalem to serve the saints;
26. 因為 馬其頓 省和 亞該亞 省的信徒，樂意與 耶路撒冷 聖徒中的窮人有一些分享 。 for Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution to the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
27. 確實，他們是樂意的，不過這也是他們的責任，因為外邦人如果分享了 猶太 人屬靈的事，也就應該在物質的事 上服事 猶太 人。 Yes, they were pleased, and they are indebted to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual benefits, then they are obligated to minister to Jews in material needs.
28. 所以，當我完成了這件事，向他們印證了這事的成果，我就要經過你們那裡，往 西班牙 去。 So when I have finished this and safely delivered the funds to them, I will go by way of you to Spain.
29. 我知道，我到你們那裡去的時候，一定帶著基督豐盛完美的 祝福而去。 But I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
30. 弟兄們，藉著我們的主耶穌基督、藉著聖靈的愛，我懇求你們與我一同竭力為我向神禱告： Now I implore you, brothers, through the Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to agonize together with me in your prayers to God on my behalf:
31. 願神 救我脫離 猶太 地區不肯信從的人，也使我為 耶路撒冷 的這服事 可以蒙聖徒們的悅納， that I may be rescued from the unbelievers in Judea, that my service for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints,
32. 好讓我能照著神的旨意，快快樂樂地到你們那裡去，和你們同得安息。 and that, by God's will, I may come to you with joy and be refreshed together with you.
33. 願賜平安的神，與你們大家同在！阿們。 The God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
Romans 16
1. 我向你們推薦我們的姐妹 菲比，她是 堅革里 教會的女執事 。 I commend to you our sister Phoebe, who is a servant of the church in Cenchreae.
